title: Regularity on reduced characteristic leaves
source_hypothesis: Properly supported scalar principal-type operator of real order with smooth homogeneous principal symbol and lower-order S(1,0) remainder, satisfying condition (P); actual active reduced leaf with compact fibers.
completed_component_scope: Full Theorem 26.9.1: min(s_u,s+m-1) is superharmonic on the reduced two-dimensional characteristic leaf whenever s_Pu is at least the superharmonic s, and the conic case gives concavity on the affine ray quotient. The compact collapsed fibers, rank-two singletons and extended-valued functions are all covered.
reviewed_arguments: The full scalar Theorem 26.9.1 is proved, including every real operator order, the actual reduced complex leaf and the conic affine conclusion. The active quotient uses its exact compact maximal fibers and proper local charts; it is not a substitute quotient.
The infimum regularity on a compact fiber is lower semicontinuous by local properness and has a finite local Sobolev lower bound. Endpoint Sobolev membership is never inferred from an index supremum.

The homogeneous normal form is valid on a common neighborhood of the whole fiber. Exact elliptic order reducers and inverse canonical graph operators transport every real Sobolev index with the required m-minus-one shift.

The scalar exponential gauge uses the full S0 remainder along all high-frequency rays. Every normalized derivative is uniform, and cancellation holds on the entire collapsed interval or at the rank-two singleton. No homogeneous lower-order limit is needed.

The corrected full time-space coefficient estimate handles collapsed intervals. A separate short-time proof uses the exact Nirenberg–Treves constant and bounded finite products when the coefficient is positive at a rank-two point, including conic leaves.
A full-spacetime shell-dependent remainder has a small operator norm by the fixed-width scalar norm estimate. Both solution and coefficient-gradient estimates survive its absorption.

The real flow chart is used only to construct scalar weights. The parameter-uniform degenerate complex coordinate retains the full compact time interval, and its invariant quadratic normal factor has exact positive distance bounds.

A compact quotient disk has a compact inverse image. The cutoff derivative on the leaf lies in a boundary collar. Lower semicontinuity and finite distribution bounds give one finite normal damping constant for all three strict inequalities.

The finite symbol expansion acts on the actual H-minus-M distribution. Its depth exceeds one plus the largest real weight plus M and a positive margin. All logarithmic factors, separated supports and polynomially weighted tails are controlled.

The full normalized spacetime bracket includes minus alpha_t times phi_sigma. Its sign is explicit, and the factorized complete commutator uses precisely the time, transverse base and frequency coefficient operators in the corrected estimate.

The complete remainder commutator has one extra frequency factor. The source comparison, square-root times logarithm absorption and exact variable-index converse give the required index at every point of the compact fiber.

The finite bootstrap uses half-order increments, so its one-order assumption remains strict at every step. Polynomial comparison then gives every harmonic comparison and the intrinsic superharmonic conclusion.

The conic conclusion includes both directions of the extended-valued concavity equivalence. Truncation, radial convolution, exact circle means, pointwise recovery and real-affine transition maps are proved explicitly.

Three complete solutions check a time-only coefficient commutator, an oscillating frequency-dependent gauge and a smooth flat collapsed interval with an exact positive normal barrier. The illustration uses their exact coordinate formulas.
Twenty-four finite algebraic checks, 368 parsed formulae, 32 numbered displays and seventeen inspected lesson captures support review; none substitutes for the complete analytic arguments.

The one-dimensional descent, later semi-concavity and solvability arguments, general-manifold scalar observation assembly and internal foundation closure remain active. No full Section 26.9 or full-course completion is claimed.
